- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent price is trending up.
- Model consistently overpredicts after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 0.5–1.5% from forecast 2–3 days post-spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive forecasts are above true outcome, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period momentum; if sentiment turns bullish late in history, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% for final 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; add 0.3–0.7% to forecast if sentiment shifts from bearish to bullish mid-horizon.
